patch_description: The original program was deeply broken: `recursive_reorder` built DataFrames with mismatched columns, mutated grouped copies, renamed columns mid-recursion, returned empty `column_orderings`, sorted the final frame after permuting rows (breaking row identity vs. per-row orders), and asserted on shapes it could not guarantee — validation failed on those datasets. The fix replaces the whole editable block with a simple, correct algorithm aligned with the actual objective (character-Trie prefix reuse): serialize every cell exactly (NaN → ""), build up to three cheap candidate orderings (original order, global frequency-ranked order by len(v)*count*(count-1), and a bounded conditional partition tree giving per-row orders), score each candidate with the exact serial-Trie reuse (sum of adjacent LCPs over sorted serialized rows, computed via binary search so comparisons run in C), and return the best. All rows/values are preserved; per-row column orderings are consistent with the returned data; col_merge and one_way_dep are honored via the existing parent API semantics.
